This method attempts to convert a country name to its ISO 2 code based on the provided country name. It first trims the input string to remove any leading or trailing whitespace. If the trimmed string is null, it returns null. If the string length is 2, it directly returns the string as it is. If the string length is 3, it attempts to find the ISO 2 code using the `LocaleUtils.getCountryISO2FromISO3` method. If the ISO 2 code is found, it returns it. If the ISO 2 code is not found, it iterates through all available ISO 2 codes and their translations to find a match with the input country name. If a match is found, it returns the corresponding ISO 2 code. If no match is found after checking all possible ISO 2 codes, it returns null.

This method takes an ISO3 code as input and returns the corresponding ISO2 code. It first trims the input string to remove any leading or trailing whitespace. If the input string is null or has a length of 0, it returns null. Otherwise, it iterates over all available ISO2 codes using `Locale.getISOCountries()`. For each ISO2 code, it creates a `Locale` object and retrieves the corresponding ISO3 code using `getISO3Country()`. If the retrieved ISO3 code matches the input ISO3 code, it returns the corresponding ISO2 code. If no match is found after checking all ISO2 codes, it returns null.

This method attempts to convert a country name to its ISO 3 code based on the provided country name. It first trims the input string to remove any leading or trailing whitespace. If the trimmed string is null, it returns null. If the string length is 3, it directly returns the string as it is assumed to be an ISO 3 code. If the string length is 2, it attempts to find the corresponding ISO 3 code using the `LocaleUtils.getCountryISO3FromISO2` method. If no ISO 3 code is found, it iterates through all available ISO 2 codes, creating a `Locale` object for each, and checks if the display country name of the `Locale` matches the input country name. If a match is found, it returns the corresponding ISO 3 code. If no match is found after checking all possible ISO 2 codes, it returns null.
